featured_discoveries.title: How Nature Builds 10,000 Fishes: Resolving D'Arcy Thompson's 1917 Transformation Paradox Across 10,303 Species
featured_discoveries.author: Joel Dietz
featured_discoveries.tldr_13yo: Global growth rules (D'Arcy Thompson's curved rubber sheet) shape the outside of a fish for swimming over 150 million years (94%–99% alignment across 440 families), while competition with neighbors rewires the jaws and snout on the inside (3.3× to 9.3× faster) so sister species can share the same coral reef without fighting over the same food.
featured_discoveries.bioelectric_connection: Directly parallels bioelectric morphogenesis in two ways: (1) Global V_mem axial-dorsoventral gradients establish the low-dimensional coordinate field (Thompson's 8-parameter rubber sheet) across the somitic trunk and median fin folds; (2) Local neural-crest craniofacial ionocyte domains ('Picasso frog' / teleost trophic modules) act as decoupled bioelectric subroutines that rapidly rewire jaw lever mechanics under sympatric trophic competition.

featured_discoveries.title: From Bioelectric Mantle Excitation to Wolfram's Rule 30: Infinite Period-Doubling, Exact k₅ = 87,867 Horizon & Lean 4 Neural-Gate Isomorphism
featured_discoveries.author: Joel Dietz
featured_discoveries.tldr_13yo: Proves in Lean 4 that the Ermentrout–Campbell–Oster (1986) neurosecretory mantle threshold equation is bit-for-bit isomorphic to Wolfram's Rule 30 cellular automaton, proves unconditionally that left-cone period-doubling never cycles (lim P_k = ∞), and resolves the exact unit-seed P = 16 → 32 horizon at diagonal k₅ = 87,867.
